item.title: Trump Administration Launches Hunt For Noncitizen Voter Fraud Before Midterms
item.description: Election fraud is exceedingly rare, but President Trump has fixated on rooting it out this year, claiming without evidence that tens of thousands of noncitizens are registered to vote.
item.dc:creator: Nick Corasaniti and Hamed Aleaziz
item.media:credit: Valerie Plesch for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Department of Homeland Security is scouring state voter rolls for evidence of fraud ahead of the November elections.

item.title: Trump Returns to a Familiar Playbook as the War With Iran Flares Up Again
item.description: The United States seems increasingly bogged down in Iran after six months of conflict, despite President Trump’s declarations of military dominance.
item.dc:creator: Erica L. Green
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:credit: Demetrius Freeman for The New York Times
item.media:description: President Trump said in a social media post on Tuesday night that he “couldn’t care less” about an agreement with Iran, hours after a U.S. attack.

item.title: U.S.S. Abraham Lincoln Docks in Thailand, Giving Weary Crew a Break
item.description: Thousands of sailors and Marines serve on the U.S.S. Abraham Lincoln, which came into the spotlight because of a tough deployment in the war in Iran.
item.dc:creator: Richard C. Paddock and Phuriphat Dejsuphong
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:credit: Anthony Wallace/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
item.media:description: Crew members on the flight deck of the U.S.S. Abraham Lincoln as it arrived at the port of Laem Chabang near Pattaya, Thailand, on Wednesday.

item.title: U.S. and Iran Survey the Damage After a Night of Intense Strikes
item.description: The American military said its barrage was retaliation against recent attacks on U.S. forces and marine traffic. Iranian officials said a wedding was hit and civilians killed.
item.dc:creator: Yeganeh Torbati
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:credit: Iranian Red Crescent Society, via Reuters
item.media:description: A still from a video provided by the Iranian Red Crescent rescue service showed damage in Kuhestak, southern Iran, on Wednesday.

item.title: How the Met’s Galliano Show Fell Apart
item.description: Anna Wintour put her full power and prestige behind a designer convicted of an antisemitic hate crime. Behind the scenes, influential New Yorkers revolted.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Bernstein, Vanessa Friedman and Dana Rubinstein
item.media:credit: Lucia Vazquez for The New York Times
item.media:description: One high-level donor called the Metropolitan Museum of Art’s plan to honor the designer John Galliano “insane.”

item.title: Deadlocked Jury in Lindsay Clancy Trial Again Says It Can’t Reach a Verdict
item.description: After roughly 30 hours of debate, jurors told the judge for a second time that they couldn’t reach unanimous agreement. He sent them back for one last try.
item.dc:creator: Maia Spoto and Mark Arsenault
item.media:credit: Pool photo by Greg Derr
item.media:description: Lindsay Clancy doesn’t deny killing her children in 2023, but she has mounted an insanity defense.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy’s Trial Prompts Patients and Doctors to Rethink Postpartum Care
item.description: Requests for advice from women with maternal mental health conditions, as well as health providers who care for them, have surged.
item.dc:creator: Pam Belluck
item.media:credit: Pool photo by Greg Derr

item.title: What Is ‘Narrative Art?’ The Lucas Museum Finally Shows Us Its Vision.
item.description: After several delays, George Lucas’s legacy project is finally ready to open. There’s less “Star Wars” than you might expect.
item.dc:creator: Matt Stevens, Robin Pogrebin and Adam Amengual
item.media:description: The Lucas Museum of Narrative Art intends to present the images and objects that make stories come alive.

item.title: In Nepal and Tibet, Pollution on Glaciers Could Fuel More Flood Disasters
item.description: Darkened by soot from vehicles and factories, the region’s glaciers are absorbing more heat and melting at dangerous rates.
item.dc:creator: Hiroko Tabuchi
item.category: Far East, South and Southeast Asia and Pacific Areas
item.media:credit: Jason Gulley for The New York Times
item.media:description: A meltwater lake on the Ngozumpa Glacier in Nepal in 2025.

item.title: The ‘Miracle House’ That Survived Nepal’s Floods
item.description: People are coming to take photos of the green-painted house, which kept the Pyakurel family safe as the area all around them was destroyed by rampaging floodwaters.
item.dc:creator: Mujib Mashal and Binod Ghimire
item.media:credit: Arun Sankar/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images

item.title: In a Big Win, Google Won’t Have to Break Up Its Ad Tech Business, Court Rules
item.description: In a long-awaited decision, a federal judge said Google must change its ad tech business to address antitrust issues, but did not disclose the measures.
item.dc:creator: David McCabe and Tripp Mickle
item.media:credit: Lucia Vazquez for The New York Times
item.media:description: The government had asked the court to require Google to sell off parts of its business.

item.title: Woman Killed in Times Square Stabbing Identified as Bank of America VP
item.description: The New York Police Department is still trying to piece together what led a 49-year-old woman to stab two strangers, one fatally.
item.dc:creator: Maria Cramer, Chelsia Rose Marcius and Mark Bonamo
item.media:credit: Todd Heisler/The New York Times
item.media:description: A knife-wielding 49-year-old woman attacked two people in Times Square before she was shot and fatally wounded by the police.

item.title: ‘Don’t Worry About Me’: Attacker’s Father Thought She Had Turned a Corner
item.description: Pamela Cisneros was killed by the police in Times Square after she stabbed two people, one fatally. Her father said she had stopped going with him to her mental health appointments.
item.dc:creator: Chelsia Rose Marcius, Miles G. Cohen, Amy Julia Harris and Katelyn Ferral
item.media:credit: Todd Heisler/The New York Times
item.media:description: Pamela Cisneros fatally stabbed a 32-year-old woman and wounded a 68-year-old man in Times Square on Monday, the police said.

item.title: Times Square Police Shooting Was Justified but Put Others at Risk, Experts Say
item.description: Officers who stood around a woman wielding two kitchen knives, and then opened fire without clearing the area, risked harming themselves or passers-by, the experts said.
item.dc:creator: Andy Newman
item.media:credit: Todd Heisler/The New York Times
item.media:description: The police said a woman stabbed two people in Times Square on Monday, killing a 32-year-old woman.

item.title: Leanne Morgan, the 60-Year-Old Breakout Comedy Star
item.description: The homey Southern comic is a red-state phenomenon with blue-state celebrity, big tours, a Netflix series and Judd Apatow’s adoration. How did she get here?
item.dc:creator: Ginia Bellafante
item.media:credit: Jared Soares for The New York Times

item.title: As Trump Throws a Midterm Party, Some Vulnerable Republicans Send Regrets
item.description: Many members of Congress in the most competitive re-election races are skipping the chance to share a pep rally stage with President Trump.
item.dc:creator: Annie Karni, Michael Gold and Luke Broadwater
item.media:credit: Francis Chung/POLITICO, via Associated Press
item.media:description: Representative David Valadao of California said that President Trump had a part to play in the midterm elections, but that navigating around a deeply unpopular president and his policies was a challenge.

item.title: Billionaires Sent Montana Prices Soaring. Can Democrats Capitalize?
item.description: For years, Democrats have failed to harness the anger of Montanans contending with out-of-state wealth driving up costs. This year, a smokejumper thinks he can succeed.
item.dc:creator: Jack Healy
item.media:credit: Will Warasila for The New York Times
item.media:description: Sam Forstag, a telegenic firefighter and union leader, is the Democratic candidate for a House race in Montana.

item.title: How New York Times Reporters Traced Dark Money in Politics
item.description: About $1 billion in anonymous contributions is coursing through midterm races across the country. Figuring out where the funds are coming from is no easy task.
item.dc:creator: Mike Abrams, Theodore Schleifer and Amy Gardner
item.media:credit: Travis Dove for The New York Times
item.media:description: Political campaigns are awash in money with obscured origins.

item.title: Inside the Fight Against a Flesh-Eating Fly in Mexico
item.description: For the first time in a year, the U.S.-Mexico border partly reopened to cattle imports following a screwworm infestation across the region. The battle against the flesh-eating fly has only just begun deep in Mexico.
item.dc:creator: James Wagner and Luis Antonio Rojas
item.media:credit: Luis Antonio Rojas for The New York Times
item.media:description: New World screwworm flies in a cage at a facility in Metapa, Mexico, that that produces sterile flies, which when released into the wild slowly reduce the population size.
